## v2.7.0 Release notes

This release brings together the features, fixes, and maintenance changes since v2.6.0. It adds an AI assistant and Mux companion, experimental aggregation hotspot, rule-set subscriptions, adaptive speed and latency-first scheduling, MTU diagnostics, and stable/preview update channels. It also improves Steam download node optimization, TUN compatibility, configuration persistence, and desktop interactions.

### AI assistant and external MCP

- Added a dedicated assistant workspace for conversations, model configuration, external AI connections, and companion appearance. It shares conversations and task state with the in-app floating Mux companion.
- Supports OpenAI-compatible Chat Completions and Responses, plus Anthropic Messages, with selectable authentication. Accepts host roots, custom prefixes, and complete endpoint URLs. Remote services require HTTPS; loopback services may use HTTP.
- Fetch and search model lists or enter a model ID manually. Save and test tool calling verifies the model capabilities needed to operate the application.
- The assistant can inspect status, adapters, connection summaries, and redacted diagnostics; configure mode, participating adapters, four scheduling strategies, and weights; manage individual routing rules; and start or stop aggregation. Tools also cover NAT/STUN, Steam optimization, starting/stopping a saved hotspot, and WFP/BFE repair. Capability reporting identifies functions that still require the UI.
- Messages include the current page name and selected routing-rule context. Navigating away neither changes an already submitted task's target nor stops its background work.
- Distinguishes routine operations from actions requiring confirmation. External MCP writes retain in-app confirmation. Configuration changes invalidate pending approvals based on stale state.
- Added a local Streamable HTTP MCP service, disabled and read-only by default. When enabled, it uses loopback networking and a temporary access key. It does not configure other AI clients automatically or expose general command execution or arbitrary file access.
- API keys and local conversation history are encrypted for the current Windows user. Changing the service address, protocol, authentication, model, or key isolates the new context so old conversations are not automatically sent to a new service.
- Improved multi-step tool calling with reasoning models by preserving the protocol fields required within a task. Improved configuration recovery and errors without automatically retrying operations that could execute twice.
- Unified assistant configuration and conversation layouts, Markdown rendering, tool progress, and approval cards. Fixed replayed replies after navigation, misaligned reply/thinking states, input remaining open after approval, and returning to an outdated chat position.

### Mux companion and personalization

- Added a draggable in-app companion with message input, reply summaries, access to full conversations, processing state, and approval prompts. Its visibility can be controlled in settings.
- Added the Mux wardrobe to import, preview, apply, and export `.muxskin`/ZIP packages, or create a skin from a transparent PNG. Includes size, animation, speech-bubble anchor, and reset controls.
- Supports PNG/sprite animations, layered characters, and Cubism 3/4 Live2D models, with idle, thinking, approval, reply, hover, and drag states. Images provide a fallback when model loading fails.
- Moved skin parsing to a background Worker and preserve character instances across navigation. Improved resource handling for hidden pages, disabled animations, and WebGL context restoration to reduce repeated loading and UI stalls.
- Refined light/dark themes, built-in and local backgrounds, materials, and appearance settings, including local preference persistence and navigation state retention.

### Aggregation hotspot (experimental)

- Added a Toolbox hotspot that shares an active TUN aggregation session through Windows Mobile Hotspot. Phones and other devices connect normally over Wi-Fi without a proxy configuration or client application.
- Added quick controls and a detail page for saved SSID, password, and band settings, random password generation, password copying, locally generated Wi-Fi QR codes, connected devices, and sharing diagnostics.
- Hotspot passwords are encrypted for the current Windows user and excluded from command lines and general logs. Fixed stale UI drafts showing a different password or QR code when AI or another entry point starts the saved hotspot.
- Automatic band selection prefers 5 GHz when supported and may retry with Windows automatic selection after specific failures when the hotspot is confirmed off. Explicit 5 GHz requests report failures without silently changing bands.
- Improved TUN profile discovery on Windows 10, recognition of Wi-Fi 7 and vendor-named wireless adapters, and compatibility with older band APIs.
- Distinguishes hotspot readiness from verified sharing egress. A ready hotspot remains available with an unverified-egress indication when legacy ICS enumeration is temporarily unavailable. Added gateway, sharing-interface, configured-band, and link-rate diagnostics.
- Improved startup waits, failure retries, shutdown confirmation, and restoration of the original configuration. Shared operation locks prevent duplicate actions across the card and detail page. Fixed late status results overwriting shutdown state and failures preventing subsequent retries.
- Stops the hotspot before stopping aggregation. Missing TUN, an invalid gateway, or a confirmed wrong egress ends sharing instead of falling back to another physical adapter. Existing Windows hotspots or other ICS sessions are not automatically taken over.

### Scheduling and forwarding performance

- Scheduling strategies and adapter weights can be changed while running, preserving established connections' egress bindings. Persistence failures attempt to restore the previous scheduling configuration, and unsupported Core capabilities are reported explicitly.
- Added Adaptive speed: starts with even allocation, gradually adjusts new-connection shares using sustained throughput and actual connection turnover, and retains a minimum share per eligible adapter. Insufficient demand keeps allocation balanced; a significant aggregate-throughput drop triggers rollback and cooldown.
- Fixed excessive preference for one adapter, starvation of low-share adapters, and temporary IPv4/IPv6 or health-filter candidate changes repeatedly resetting global learning. Existing round-robin and manual-weight strategies retain their own behavior.
- Added Low latency first: selects links using target-probe latency, jitter, and loss, with reference probes as fallback estimates. Hold times and improvement thresholds reduce unnecessary switching.
- Under latency-first scheduling, UDP can rebuild its upstream after missing replies when repeated probe failures and a usable alternative provide supporting evidence. Historical packets are not replayed; healthy flows and established TCP connections are not actively migrated.
- Improved scheduling state, learning-phase, effective-strategy, and allocation-share reporting, distinguishing connection shares from bandwidth shares.
- Reused UDP reply buffers and improved TCP relay buffer lifetimes to reduce allocations. Fixed pool updates disrupting the original rotation order.

### Routing and rule-set subscriptions

- Added reject rules for processes, domains, and IP addresses, including priority handling, enable/disable controls, and hot reload.
- Added TUN rule-set subscriptions that bind a whole domain/IP category to an outbound. Supported match types can be imported from Clash payload YAML and sing-box source JSON instead of entering every rule manually.
- Subscription management supports creation, editing, enable/disable, deletion, updates, and priorities, with update state, entry counts, and ignored-entry counts. Entries can be searched and paginated; forms, action feedback, and list refresh behavior were refined.
- Subscription downloads require public HTTPS endpoints, with redirect, size, and time limits, conditional requests, normalization, and deduplication. Redirects and DNS resolution cannot redirect downloads into localhost or private networks.
- External rules with unsupported inversion, port conditions, or logical nesting are ignored as a whole and counted, instead of stripping conditions and changing their routing meaning.
- Content and priority changes support hot reload. Changes requiring main-configuration declarations, including new subscriptions or outbound rebinding, prompt for a restart. Improved failed-update rollback, deleted/disabled rule publication, and adapter-specific outbounds.
- Fixed null empty lists crashing the panel, empty IP arrays failing parsing, and premature removal of disabled subscriptions' cached content preventing re-enablement.
- Quick-add routing from active connections now preserves custom match order and checks configuration revisions to avoid overwriting concurrent AI/MCP or UI edits. New outbound conflicts require renewed confirmation; save errors stay inside the dialog and preserve the draft.
- Improved focus retention during batch previews, routing tables and toolbars, and selection/scroll state after saving, deleting, or navigating.

### Steam download node optimization

- Validates a small number of candidate nodes concurrently so verified candidates can start trials without waiting for earlier slow nodes. Probe traffic, concurrency, and candidate limits remain bounded.
- Added conditional early trials for verified candidates while retaining original-route comparison connections. Original-node changes, expired samples, and connection failures clear stale scores so pre-pause throughput does not bias later decisions.
- Added cooldown protection for sustained moderate degradation while retaining severe-slowdown fallback. Existing candidates can be revalidated when the pool is full, without interrupting established downloads.
- The detail page distinguishes disabled, waiting for engine, incompatible Core, waiting for downloads, validating, learning, and preferred-node states.
- Added node search/filtering, valid-sample and failure details, recent overall/switched throughput, cumulative traffic, cache state, update time, and Core version information.
- Improved refresh, retry, and re-evaluation feedback. Stale requests cannot overwrite a new learning session, and traffic statistics are not presented as speed-improvement percentages.

### TUN, DNS, and network diagnostics

- Updated the bundled official Windows sing-box to **1.14.2**, including source and checksum records.
- TUN shutdown first requests a graceful sing-box exit before bounded forced cleanup, preserving FakeIP metadata during immediate restarts and cached-only resolution.
- Improved TUN address and route checks to reduce false conflicts from backup VPN routes, Windows IPv6 transition interfaces, and unrelated networks. Expanded local-network and route-change diagnostics.
- Normal startup treats overlapping third-party tunnel routes and unreachable public test sites as diagnostic information. Public-probe failures after startup or during operation no longer independently stop the engine.
- Improved force-start behavior by skipping external connectivity tests and some environmental inference while still avoiding known local interface addresses. Missing runtime files, no valid adapter, duplicate source addresses, insufficient permissions, and actual TUN creation failures still fail explicitly.
- DNS fallback reads the running Core configuration and preserves encrypted-DNS policy and egress binding. Fixed resolution not retaining an explicitly selected adapter. Elevated desktop compatibility is now informational, reducing unnecessary startup blocks.
- Added MTU probing, confirmed application, and original-value restoration to network diagnostics, requiring network services to be stopped first. Probes use a selected adapter and IPv4 target; expired results or changed adapter configuration cannot be applied. Original values are saved before changes and remain available after reopening the application.
- MTU changes run through the elevated Core with read-back verification and affect only the current IPv4 active configuration. Improved diagnostic status, cancellation, and error feedback.

### Desktop interactions, stability, and maintenance

- Active connections can be grouped by process or adapter, with improved summaries, expansion, sorting, and quick routing. Virtualized large lists reduce rendering overhead at high connection counts.
- Navigation preserves searches, selections, drafts, and scroll positions. Inactive pages pause unnecessary polling, and stale asynchronous results no longer overwrite newer state after returning.
- Refined Home adapter cards, allocation feedback, speed displays, and English layouts to reduce shifting as values change. Improved virtual-adapter recognition, including Radmin VPN.
- Improved tray window styling, typography, spacing, keyboard focus, and placement near the click. Fixed touch popup positioning and added touchscreen title-bar dragging.
- Unified notification, dropdown, dialog, and hotspot-form layouts across narrow windows and themes. Settings-load failures now show an explicit error and retry action.
- Settings preferences merge by field so language/appearance changes do not overwrite unsaved network edits or another service's recent changes. Improved adapter/settings save queues and concurrent-write protection.
- Fixed Windows Core named-pipe handle races and communication stability issues. Extended capability negotiation and protocol regression coverage for scheduling, hotspot, and MTU operations.
- In-place installation prioritizes the user's existing custom install directory instead of unexpectedly reverting to the default path.
- Fixed website submodule mapping and synchronized its source reference. Added documentation for AI, hotspot, scheduling, MTU, skin authoring, and release versioning.
- Updated frontend dependencies and lockfiles. Expanded tests for subscriptions, FakeIP restarts, concurrent saves, skin lifetimes, hotspot recovery, and UI interactions, and stabilized several asynchronous tests on Windows CI.

### Versions and update channels

- Added Stable / Preview (Beta / RC) in settings, defaulting to Stable with a persisted preference. Preview checks both stable and prerelease feeds and selects the newest version.
- Supports numeric prerelease ordering through `beta.N → rc.N → stable`. Switching back to Stable does not automatically downgrade; updates resume when a stable release with the same base version or a higher version is available.
- Beta/RC releases use a separate signed update channel and are marked as prereleases without replacing stable latest. Older clients continue using the original stable feed.
- Added a shared version-setting and consistency-check command for the UI, Core, updater, and Windows metadata. Release builds inject the tag version and keep display versions separate from four-part numeric Windows versions.

### Upgrade and usage notes

- This is the **v2.7.0 stable release** for Windows 10/11 x64. Use the official installer to update both desktop and Core, then restart aggregation/TUN to apply the new runtime and main configuration.
- AI features require a user-configured model service with tool calling; providers may charge for API use. Conversations and necessary tool results are sent to the selected service. Mux currently appears only inside HypoMux.
- Aggregation hotspot remains experimental and requires Windows Mobile Hotspot support and an active TUN session. Drivers, radio bands, sharing state, and upstream networks affect results.
- Aggregation, adaptive scheduling, and Steam optimization do not guarantee faster downloads or split one TCP connection across links. Latency-first failover may change the public egress and cannot guarantee uninterrupted game sessions. MTU results apply only to the selected adapter-to-target path.
- Rule-set content and priorities support hot reload. Restart TUN when prompted after operations such as adding a subscription or changing its outbound. Older versions differ in support for new configuration features; back up settings and rules before planning a rollback.
- Official GitHub and Tencent CNB downloads continue to distribute the same signed installer. Automatic updates retain Ed25519 manifest, installer size, SHA-256, and Windows Authenticode verification.

> Thanks to SignPath.io for providing Windows code-signing services for HypoMux, and to SignPath Foundation for issuing the project's open-source code-signing certificate.
